candidates.statement: Checkout 502s originate downstream: order calls payment, which returns 503 Service Unavailable, and order surfaces 502 to gateway. Inventory reservations succeed (200), so the failure is in the payment authorization path, not inventory or redis.
candidates.uncertainty: Payment-side logs/metrics excluded; root cause within payment (config, saturation) not established.

report.explanation: Traces show consistent pattern: inventory reservation 200, payment authorization 503, order returns 502, gateway checkout 502. Gateway metrics show ~10.7 502s on /v1/checkout in 60s. Topology confirms gateway->order->payment. Fault is downstream of gateway in the payment authorization path; payment-side evidence is excluded, so the specific payment fault is not yet bounded.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs and metrics for /v1/authorizations 503s during the window
Order service logs showing why payment 503 is mapped to 502
Payment dependency topology and resource saturation data
